newsitem.title: FRANCE: Top Paris policeman suspended in political case.
newsitem.headline: Top Paris policeman suspended in political case.

text.p: A Paris court on Monday ordered the suspension of a senior police officer for refusing to help a judge investigating alleged official corruption during President Jacques Chirac's term as mayor of the French capital.

But it decided not to press legal charges against the man, Olivier Foll, head of the Paris CID (criminal investigation division). Foll appealed against the suspension, for six months, and his lawyer said he would remain at work until it was heard.

Foll had ordered his men not to help anti-corruption judge Eric Halphen search the home of Mayor Jean Tiberi in July in an inquiry into the finances of Chirac's Rally for the Republic (RPR) Gaullist party.
Halphen had to search Tiberi's home on his own. Magistrates and opposition leaders demanded Foll be punished but Gaullist Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre expressed support for him.
Dozens of senior police officers were present in court to show solidarity with Foll when his case was heard on Monday.

Halphen has for months been investigating allegations that kickbacks were paid to the RPR in connection with housing contracts in the Paris area. Chirac was mayor of Paris until his election as president last year.

Foll's lawyer Jean-Marc Varaut said when the case first came up in court that his client had withdrawn the officers from the case because Halphen only told them outside the building that they were going to search Tiberi's home.
He said Halphen's attitude showed he mistrusted the police. He also said Halphen had not followed correct legal procedures when requisitioning police for the search.
The French media say Halphen feared police officers assigned to help him had spied on his investigations for their superiors in order to delay investigations uncomfortably close to Chirac.
The court chose not to take any action against Foll's deputy, Philippe Prunier.
